correctness.rationale: Probability-normalized power-weight Bergman monomial norms are gamma-ratio moments. For any positive angular measure the Gram diagonal is w_k r^(2k), whence a universal condition-number lower bound by Rayleigh. Strict log-concavity of w_k t^k forces endpoint minima, giving a unique minimax balancing radius. Equality requires the first monomial basis vector to be a minimal-eigenvalue eigenvector and hence all first N angular moments zero, which is sufficient; exactly N+1 positive nodes force a unitary weighted Fourier matrix and a regular polygon with uniform weights. Gamma ratio asymptotics and exact ratio localization give K ~ e^(-a)/Gamma(a+1) (N/log N)^a for a=alpha+1. The standard-library checker passed 920 finite checks. Finite checks do not establish the infinite limit or the exact theorem.

value.rationale: Finite-dimensional Bergman MZ sampling needs quantitatively stable evaluation schemes. The theorem determines the exact best achievable two-sided condition number among all one-circle sensor designs, with a uniquely optimal radial location, a complete equality classification even under oversampling and explicit alpha-dependent divergence. This quantitatively separates one-radius and disk-wide MZ sampling in a way not implied by a cardinality-only or qualitative sampling theorem; the precise power-logarithmic exponent and coefficient inform radial sensor placement and conditioning of polynomial reconstruction.
